subject: Re: Snowbird collaboration — whitebox distribution & co-billing
messages:
From: Ari Levin <ari@snowbird.ai>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 21 Feb 2027 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Snowbird x Redwood — whitebox embed and co-billing interest

Hi Sean,

Nice to meet you — we spoke briefly at the AI Platform Summit booth. Snowbird is exploring a whitebox option to embed a high‑performance inference runtime into our analytics product so our customers can enable LLM features in a fully branded experience. A few points on our side: 

- We expect a mix of 100-500 active tenants in year one, many low‑qps but some bursty workflows.
- We care about branding control (no Redwood logo in UI), per-tenant telemetry separation, and an optional co-billing model where Snowbird presents a single invoice to our customers and we handle remittance to Redwood.
- Security: enterprise SSO + optional on‑prem runtime for a subset of regulated customers.

I attached a short integration outline (snowbird-integration-outline.pdf). Would love to schedule a 30m call next week to run through feasibility and commercial models. Who on your side should we loop in for billing/legal and technical feasibility?

Thanks,
Ari Levin
Head of Partnerships, Snowbird AI
ari@snowbird.ai

Attachment: snowbird-integration-outline.pdf
From: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>
To: Ari Levin <ari@snowbird.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 22 Feb 2027 10:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Snowbird x Redwood — whitebox embed and co-billing interest

Hi Ari — great to meet you over email and thanks for the outline. I'm Sean (partnerships). Looping in Marissa (commercial ops) and Priyom (product partnerships) so we can address the billing and technical questions in one go. Quick clarifying Qs before the call: 

1) When you say co-billing, do you mean Snowbird wants a single invoice to end customers and then Snowbird remits to Redwood (gross billing), or you want us to bill end customers on Snowbird's behalf (pass-through)?
2) For the tenant scale above, do you expect most traffic to use our hosted inference or will you require private/on‑prem images for a meaningful subset?
3) Any specific compliance requirements (SOC 2, data residency) for the initial set of customers?

I'm available Tue/Wed next week between 10:00-14:00 PT — I can send a calendar invite. Proposed agenda: 1) technical feasibility & deployment modes, 2) commercial models (revenue share vs reseller), 3) draft timeline for a POC.

Cheers,
Sean Gallagher
Director, Partnerships | Redwood Inference
sean.gallagher@redwood.com

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>

Date: Tue, 23 Feb 2027 14:45:00 -0800
Subject: Fwd: Snowbird x Redwood — whitebox embed and co-billing interest

Hi Ari — thanks for the intro and Sean for looping us in. 

Forwarding our internal sketch of the commercial options — see attached "co-billing-options.xlsx". High level: 

- Option A: Reseller license (Snowbird buys a seat/throughput commitment, bills your customers directly, Redwood invoices Snowbird monthly). Simple but Redwood doesn't maintain end-customer contracts.
- Option B: Revenue share + co-billing (Snowbird invoices customers; we track metered usage and settle monthly; Redwood issues a consolidated invoice to Snowbird for the platform fee + usage). Typically requires stronger PSI/telemetry alignment.
- Option C: Referral + hosted (Snowbird refers customers; Redwood bills end customers; simpler but less margin capture for Snowbird).

Operational asks: procurement contact, expected PO cadence, and whether Snowbird can accept monthly net-30 settlements or needs net-60. Also flagging potential sales crediting questions for our finance team.

If helpful, we can produce a short SOW template and draft commercial term sheet to fast-track legal review. 

Best,
Marissa Cole
Head of Commercial Ops | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com

Attachment: co-billing-options.xlsx

Hi all — quick technical note to add context for the call. From our side the whitebox model is feasible, but we should align on these guardrails upfront: 

- Branding: we can ship runtime artifacts with no Redwood UI bits; runtime SDK will include an attribution header unless customer requests opt-out (needs contract language).
- Telemetry & billing: for co-billing we need a clear telemetry contract (what metrics we consume and share). Per-tenant usage export via a secure S3+signed-URL endpoint is typical.
- Isolation: per-tenant KV caches and optional namespace-level encryption (customer keys) for regulated customers.
- Deployment modes: hosted-managed variant (simplest), dedicated tenant pools, or on‑prem bundle for a pilot subset. Each has different SLAs and support cost.
- Quantization/latency: we can provide quantized model variants for lower cost but must validate quality on your prompt sets.

I'll bring an integration checklist to the call (attached). Prefer to scope a 6‑8 week technical POC targeting 1–2 pilot customers.

Cheers,
Priyom Das
Partner PM, Product Partnerships | Redwood Inference
priyom.das@redwood.com

Attachment: integration-checklist.md
